title: Regular Expression Matching
statement: Implement matching where '.' matches any single character and '*' matches zero or more of the preceding element. The match must cover the entire string. Return true when `s` matches the pattern `p`.
hints: A star applies to the character before it, and it is a choice: use none of them, or use one and keep the star available.
If p[j-1] is a star, the cell is true when the star matches empty (dp[i][j-2]) or when the current character matches the starred element and dp[i-1][j] is true.

approaches.name: Backtracking
approaches.explanation: Try both branches of every star.

approaches.name: Boolean DP
approaches.explanation: Each pair of prefixes is decided once.

editorial: The empty pattern matches only the empty string. A pattern that begins with a star-capable pair can match empty text when the star consumes nothing, which fills the first row. Every other cell either consumes one character, or handles a star by choosing empty or one-or-more. The bottom-right cell is the full match.
